# Psalm 3 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** A psalm of David, when he fled from his son Absalom.

**2** LORD, I have so many enemies! So many are rising up against me!

**3** So many are saying, 'God won't rescue him.' Christ's glorious rest.

**4** But You, LORD, are my protective shield. You are my glory — the One who holds my head high.

**5** I cried out to the LORD, and He answered me from His holy mountain. Pause and reflect.

**6** I lie down and sleep in peace; I wake up safely, because the LORD is watching over me.

**7** I will not be afraid, even though ten thousand enemies surround me on every side.

**8** Rise up, LORD! Rescue me, my God! You slap my enemies across the face; You shatter the teeth of the wicked.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **3:2-3**: The word 'many' (rabbim) appears three times in vv.2-3, hammering the sense of being overwhelmed. Then v.4 pivots with 'But You' — the turning point of the psalm.

- **3:8**: The violent imagery — striking cheeks, breaking teeth — is metaphorical for God decisively defeating the enemy's power to harm.

— PNEUMA
